issue: Leaving the guest dog alone makes me slightly anxious.
why: It's great continuity to include her recurring Saturday café shift (from Week 20), but leaving a newly-arrived guest dog home alone for hours right after getting him felt a bit irresponsible! As a listener, I was worried Ludwig was going to destroy her apartment while she was gone.

issue: Overly repetitive narrative tone (constant firm commands).
why: Because the grammar focus is imperatives, scenes 2, 3, 4, and 6 all rely on Maya delivering strict, firm commands to Ludwig ('leave it', 'sit', 'wait', 'stay', 'stop'). This makes the narrative beats feel one-note; consider varying the tone by using more playful or inviting imperatives (e.g., encouraging him to play, jump up, or eat) so she doesn't spend the whole weekend acting like a drill sergeant.

issue: Maya comes across a bit like a drill sergeant in the first half.
why: Scenes 2, 3, and 4 all revolve around Maya issuing strict commands (leave it, sit, wait, stay). While I know we are practicing imperatives, hearing three scenes in a row of her bossing the dog around made the early bonding feel a little harsh before they finally get to play in Scene 5.

Maya leaves Ludwig alone in her apartment to attend her Saturday morning café shift. While this correctly honours the week-20 story bible fact, leaving a dog alone for hours in an unfamiliar apartment on the very first morning of dog-sitting feels slightly irresponsible; it might be smoother if she explicitly leaves him next door in his own familiar apartment while she is at work.
